And it\u2019s done in a way that external injuries are not visible when the suspect is produced before a magistrate.\n", "\n", "Police all over India often use it to extract information or a confession. Here\u2019s the lowdown on this illegal method of questioning a suspect: \n", "Aeroplane Ride: The hands and legs are tied behind the back. The rope is inserted to a pulley fixed to the hook on the ceiling. One side of the rope is handled by a policeman. When the rope is pulled, the criminal faces unbearable pain and supposedly \u2018reveals\u2019 the information. Lack of expertise would result in shoulder dislocation.\n", "\n", "Bombay Cut: After the criminal\u2019s hands are tied to the back, the accused is made to squat and an iron rod is inserted under his knees. Then his legs are tied and he is made to move. After every few minutes, the ropes are removed and the accused is made to walk or squat so that no external injuries are found.\n", "\n", "Hyderabadi goli: A lathi or an iron rod smeared with chilli powder is slowly pushed inside the anus. The criminals often turn unconscious.\n", "Rolling technique: The accused is made to lie down on a table with hands and legs tied. An iron pipe is kept on the back of his leg and a policeman stands on it. Two more on either sides of the pipe slowly roll it and unable to bear the pain, the accused \u2018confesses\u2019.\n", "\n", "Parrot Perch: The criminal is tied upside down. But the rule of law that underlines democracy also presupposes that once a crime is identified with a person, the law must take its course and punishment quickly visit the criminal. Only when the criminal is left with no doubt that he/she shall be called upon to repay to the society all the consequences of his/her crime, the deterrence effect can set in.\n", " \n", " The Telgi stamp and stamp paper scam made big news 15 years ago. Involvement of politicians, police officers and other public servants was alleged. The fake stamp scamster was sure of buying immunity by corrupt and other illegal means. Using money power, muscle power and political power, he repeatedly struck daring blows to many of the hallowed institutions of the great Indian democracy. In under a decade, this petty criminal progressed from being a forger to build a mafia like empire. That our present practices in our criminal justice system have no answers to stop such criminals from indulging in crime repeatedly is the real threat to our perception of rule of law. After being proclaimed as an offender by the Esplanade Court in Mumbai, the accused got released from another state high court on conditional bail, only to violate the bail conditions yet again with elsewhere.\n", " \n", " Repeated arrests of his henchmen or confinement in ", " did not in the least discourage this scamster from spreading his racket to more cities and towns. He operated with impunity from within the restrictions of the jails. He could freely approach the powers-that-be to pressurise his own gang members who wanted leave the path of crime. His retinue included corrupt police officers and others in positions of power and pelf, who could intercede on his behalf either in other police cases being registered against him or curtailing the activities of other rival gangs in the business of fake stamps and stamp papers.\n", " \n", " Some believed that when ", " superstar Dr Raj Kumar was kidnapped by the forest brigand Veerappan, Telgi was arrested to squeeze more money from him. The fake stamps scam case was entrusted to a special team named StampIT to continue investigations after the accused had been arrested and sent in 14-day police remand by the ", " City Police. Allegations of police investigations being kid gloved were being leveled. The Opposition stalled the proceedings in the legislatures demanding a CBI probe. The Karnataka government thought it fit to form a special investigation team under my leadership because of my 11-year experience in the CBI.\n", " \n", " Karnataka STAMPIT\u2019s investigations stood out among the other police investigations as a classic case of dogged pursuit of the crime and criminals within the confines of the ordinary law of the land. Launching a website to enlist public cooperation (www.stampit.info) was hardly the idea one would associate with police investigators in 2001. Not only did STAMPIT officials did this to ensure transparency in investigations, they also used the investigative tools of telephone interception, brain mapping and the like, to unravel the full ramifications of the mother of all scams. They repeatedly tried to awaken from slumber other enforcement agencies, to pursue a multidisciplinary approach to contain this nationwide malaise.\n", "\n", "\n", " \n", " Filing a dozen additional charge sheets in just the three cases that were entrusted to them for investigations, they built up their case after examining over 800 witnesses and collecting over 1000 documents. Even when the probe officials tipped off chiefs of other state police departments about huge stocks of stamps lying in their jurisdiction the responses were slow and varied.\n", " \n", " Activist Anna Hazare\u2019s writ petition in the Bombay High Court credits the Karnataka government and the STAMPIT with giving the timely tip off to the Maharashtra government about the derailment of the Pune Police investigations leading to the setting up of the Maharashtra\u2019s SIT. The case, however, got transferred to the CBI on the orders of the Apex Court for further investigations and STAMPIT had to stop its work abruptly.\n", " \n", " Now Telgi is back in the news. He is dead. But what of the crimes that he committed? What about his other partners in crime? What are the lessons for us in respect of crime investigations?\n", " \n", " Investigation is a painstaking job. The present system of investigation is mostly single investigation officer-based. After the investigation is over and the prosecution takes over, the trial lingers on for about seven to eight times longer than the case took to investigate. It is during this time that the accused get ample chance to tamper with the evidence.\n", " \n", " Before the labours of investigation can be turned into material evidence in a court of law, it is seen that the witnesses turn hostile, the complainant is won over, the prosecutor and the investigating officers get transferred and lose interest, and even trial judges are changed. The only person with sustained interest in the case and its records is the accused. Right from the time the FIR is lodged, the accused bides his/her time and slowly but surely finds ways and means to avoid being convicted of a crime in the court. The conviction rate of people involved in crimes of corruption in India is less than 4 %.\n", " \n", " Cases where the investigations are handled by a number of officers lack continuity. Disappearance of evidence is common in such cases. After the investigation phase is over, the investigators are no longer retained for assisting the prosecutor. So the field becomes free for the accused to try his/her luck. Documents and case properties routinely get mislaid.\n", " \n", " Justice delivery concentrates on protecting the rights of the accused rather than on justice to the victim. In societal crimes there is nobody to watch the interest of public. To ensure that the victim -- especially when the society is the victim, as is the case in most economic crimes and crimes of corruption -- we need to find ways and processes that ensure that evidence collected gets proved in a court of law. It is also not enough if only a few persons are arraigned in court and a majority of accused involved in the crime do not even face prosecution.\n", " \n", " The way the Panama papers were handled by the two German journalists and their newspaper Suddeutsche Zeitung is worthy of emulation in all scam related big investigations. We need to make it a team investigation with a central repository for all investigation records and collected data, duly protected with access rights etc. Each member of the investigating team will have access to all relevant case data, but no individual member would be in a position to scuttle the entire investigation. All relevant facts about an accused should get preserved digitally in a legally admissible form centrally so that a criminal gets opportunity to reform and does not graduate to more serious crimes.\n", " \n", " Reforms in Criminal Justice System are urgently needed in India. We need to work resolutely to stamp out all the inefficiencies in the criminal justice system to bring the trust back to the concept of rule of law. The section mandates that the statement of the victim (child) should be recorded by the court in 30 days of the special court taking cognisance of the offence. The HC found that in several cases, this was not followed. In many cases, the accused walked out on bail because the rule was not followed. Not to mention the stress and trauma the victims had to undergo. ", " ", " In one instance, interim bail had to be granted to an accused who had allegedly raped a four-year-old. Though the offence happened in December 2015, the child\u2019s statement was not even recorded. Since it was not recorded within 30 days as per Section 35 (1) of the Act and it was an omission by the lower court, interim bail was granted. The HC directed the Registrar General to make enquiry about the non-compliance of Section 35(1) by the lower court.", " ", " The lower court judge was transferred in May 2017, but his explanation was also recorded for the delay. The lower court claimed that it was \u201cdue to unavoidable and inevitable reasons\u201d. After the bail was granted to the accused, the trial court fixed a date for the recording of the statement of the witness. But the witnesses did not appear before the court. \u201cThe special courts shall comply the mandate of Section 35 (1) of the Act in its letter and spirit,\u201d the HC ordered.", " ", " In its judgment, the HC said, \u201cOne has to consider the situation where a child, who was of a tender age at the time of the incident, was brought before the court after a year or two and made to depose. Naturally, it would be traumatic for the child to recall the details of the horrible experience. The other side of the story could be that s/he could have been tutored under the guise of brushing his/her memory before commencement of recording of the evidence. In either way, there is likelihood of miscarriage of justice. It is said that time is the best healer, who knows that by passage of time the victim and family members may give up and may not like to submit themselves for the hassles of cross-examination and court procedure.\u201d", " ", " ", " ", " The HC made it clear that courts cannot cite lack of time or workload to delay recording of statement. He would keep saying \u201cHi Madam\u201d, \u201cYou are cute Madam\u201d, and continued this behaviour even after she implored him to stop several times. As far as the police are concerned one of the following three reasons lies at the heart of their giving wrong advice/information:\n", " \n", " 1 Incompetence (genuinely not aware).\n", " \n", " 2 Laziness (don\u2019t want the hassle).\n", " \n", " 3 Malice (have vested interest in discouraging the victim).\n", " \n", " This article is an attempt to explain some of the laws that deal with crimes against women, especially some of the changes brought about in the law via amendments in 2013 and some advice on countering the attempts by cops to stonewall a victim trying to file a first information report (FIR).\n", " \n", " \n", " \n", "\n", " \n", " Indian Penal Code Section 354A (1) which criminalises i) \u201cphysical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures\u201d, ii) \u201ca demand or request for sexual favours\u201d iii) Showing pornography against the will of a woman and iv) \u201cmaking sexually coloured remarks\u201d. The punishment for \u2018i\u2019 to \u2018iii\u2019 is minimum zero to maximum 3 years imprisonment or the payment of a fine, or both. The punishment for \u2018iv\u2019 is maximum 1 year imprisonment or a fine or both.\n", " \n", " \n", "\n", " \n", " What is unwelcome depends on the consent of the person who is being subjected to this \u2018overture\u2019. Something as simple as keeping one\u2019s hand on a woman\u2019s shoulder can be an unwelcome and sexual overture. However, there is nothing draconian about this. It is best to expressly ascertain and respect the personal physical boundaries set by every person.\n", " \n", " Let us now take a step backwards in the chronological scheme of the Indian Penal Code and discuss Section 354 (as opposed to 354A) which talks about assault or criminal use of force coupled with \u201coutraging the modesty of a woman\u201d (punishment minimum 1 year, maximum 5 years imprisonment+ mandatory fine). What constitutes the \u201coutraging of modesty\u201d and how is it different from, for instance, \u201cphysical contact and advances involving explicit overtures\u201d? The act of assaulting and disrobing a woman used to be covered under Section 354, but it is now a separate crime under 354B after amendments in 2013.\n", " \n", " \n", "\n", " \n", " In theory, the answer is that if there\u2019s an \u201cassault\u201d, it will fall under the former, if not, it falls under the latter. The purpose of this discussion regarding the difference between the two provisions is not to confound you with complicated legalese, but to mildly digress and point out that because several provisions appear to overlap and cover the same crime, corrupt cops often try to dupe a victim and draft the FIR in a manner that it results in registration of offences that attract lesser punishment.\n", " \n", " The first thing that you must do while filing a complaint is to ensure that the incident is recorded in as much detail as possible. Insist on recording the incident in words that best describe the matter according to you and don\u2019t get persuaded by cops who insist on telling you what words/sentences to use. Pertinent to point out here that even if cops do have their way and record a distorted version of what happened, this can be challenged before the court.\n", " \n", " Under Section 354B, the intentional act of assault/use of criminal force+disrobing a woman or the \u2018abetment\u2019 (enabling) of this act by someone else can lead to imprisonment of minimum 3 years and maximum 7 years, and a mandatory fine.\n", " \n", " Another addition to the Indian Penal Code via the 2013 amendment is the offence of voyeurism. Watching, recording (photographs/video) a woman engaged in a \u2018private act\u2019 or the dissemination of such image/video(s) is punishable by imprisonment for minimum 1 year and maximum 3 years plus a mandatory fine when the offence is committed for the first time, and for a minimum 3 years and maximum 7 years for every subsequent offence. The phrase \u2018private act\u2019 includes acts where the \u201cvictim\u2019s genitals, posterior or breasts are exposed or covered only in underwear; the victim is using a lavatory; or the victim is doing a sexual act that is not of a kind ordinarily done in public\u201d.\n", " \n", " Needless to add that as far as the mere act of recording is concerned, this offence gets invoked only if such recording is done without the consent of the victim and while the victim is engaged in such act in a private place where the victim has the reasonable expectation of privacy. For example, the mere act of \u2018recording\u2019 a person stripping and running on the streets is not an offence. If the victim has consented to the recording but not to the dissemination, this offence will get triggered.\n", " \n", " Getting back to the issue of stalking. It is now a criminal offence, defined as the act of following a woman and contacting her, or attempting to, to initiate a personal interaction despite a clear expression of disinterest by the woman. In case there is any ambiguity over this, a woman saying \u201cno\u201d once is sufficiently \u201cexpressing disinterest\u201d. Stalking is punishable with maximum imprisonment of 3 years at the first commission of the offence and maximum 5 years at every subsequent commission.\n", " \n", " A most welcome step has been the expansion of the definition of rape to include:\n", " \n", " i) The act of inserting the penis not only in the vagina but also in the mouth, and/or urethra of a woman.\n", " \n", " ii) Inserting any other part of the body into the anus, urethra or vagina of a woman.\n", " \n", " iii) Applying the mouth to the vagina, urethra or the anus of a woman.\n", " \n", " iv) Manipulating a woman\u2019s body in a manner to cause penetration in the anus, urethra or the vagina of the woman.\n", " \n", " v) Compelling the woman to do any of the above acts with any other person.\n", " \n", " The said acts are a crime only if they are done against the will or the consent of the woman. \u201cAgainst the will\u201d and \u201cwithout her consent\u201d are phrases used in the provision\n", " criminalising rape and the difference between the two is that the latter refers to situations where either consent is obtained by coercion or deceit. It is critical to note here that the absence of resistance by itself does not constitute consent. Without reproducing the letter of the law, I think it suffices to say that unless the woman expresses a firm and clear yes, please believe that consent is absent.\n", " \n", " Shifting focus to the procedural aspects, it is critical to know that the registration of an FIR cannot be denied on grounds of \u2018territorial jurisdiction\u2019 \u2014 an excuse cops often use. They say they are helpless as the crime did not occur in their area. The truth is they are duty bound to register a case and if territorial jurisdiction is lacking, they register what is called a \u2018Zero-FIR\u2019, which is subsequently transferred to the relevant police station.\n", " \n", " If the information about any of the aforementioned crimes (and many others such as throwing of acid) is given to the cops, their refusal to file an FIR can in fact land them in prison for a minimum period of 6 months and a maximum period of 2 years besides the payment of a mandatory fine. I often tell people that the moment cops refuse to register an FIR in any of the aforementioned cases, the first thing one should do is dial 100 and report that the police thana in question is refusing to lodge a case. You can also report the non-filing of the FIR to senior officers or to the nearest magistrate. If the victim is herself reporting the crime, the FIR must be mandatorily recorded by a woman police officer. If the victim is temporarily or permanently mentally or physically disabled, then the FIR must be recorded at the residence of the person who wants to report the offence or at a place convenient to the person. Moreover, this needs to be done in the presence of a special educator or an interpreter as the case maybe. In such cases, the process of recording the FIR must be video-graphed.\n", " \n", " It is important to remember that the FIR need not necessarily be filed by the victim and can be filed by a bystander or any person requested to do so by the victim. The police have no business questioning the authority of the person filing the FIR. The officer writing the FIR is duty bound to read the FIR back to the complainant who must make sure that he/she has noted everything correctly. If not, then corrections must be made. Finally, the complainant is entitled to a free copy of the FIR.\n", " The government of the day needs to do a lot more to make sure that more people are made aware about the provisions of such laws, failing which most of them will remain a dead letter.\n"], "title": "Puppy held in K-halli molestation case", "auth_datetime": ["Bangalore Mirror Bureau ", "|", " Updated: Jan 10, 2017, 04:00 IST"] }, { "url": "https://bangaloremirror.indiatimes.com/bangalore/crime/bangalore/crime/alert-traffic-cop-arrests-two-robbers/articleshow/56224811.cms", "content": [" In September, 2014, a traffic cop ", " (in pic) had chased and caught a notorious robber, 45-year-old Janardhana, after he was escaping after robbing a woman near the BES College. He would keep saying \u201cHi Madam\u201d, \u201cYou are cute Madam\u201d, and continued this behaviour even after she implored him to stop several times. She wondered something could be done about this. \u201cSurely a person following and saying hi/hello could not be a crime?\u201d she asked me. I dialled 100 and told the police that she was being stalked. The cops\u2019 response: \u201cIs the culprit still there? If not what can we do about it? If he isn\u2019t harming her, how is it a crime? Just ask her to ignore him and he will go away.\u201d", " ", " Stalking is a crime, but in this instance even though the letter of the law clearly spelled this out neither the victim nor the cops seemed to know that it was. As far as the police are concerned one of the following three reasons lies at the heart of their giving wrong advice/information:", " ", " 1 Incompetence (genuinely not aware).", " ", " 2 Laziness (don\u2019t want the hassle).", " ", " 3 Malice (have vested interest in discouraging the victim).", " ", " This article is an attempt to explain some of the laws that deal with crimes against women, especially some of the changes brought about in the law via amendments in 2013 and some advice on countering the attempts by cops to stonewall a victim trying to file a first information report (FIR).", " ", " Indian Penal Code Section 354A (1) which criminalises i) \u201cphysical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures\u201d, ii) \u201ca demand or request for sexual favours\u201d iii) Showing pornography against the will of a woman and iv) \u201cmaking sexually coloured remarks\u201d. The punishment for \u2018i\u2019 to \u2018iii\u2019 is minimum zero to maximum 3 years imprisonment or the payment of a fine, or both. The punishment for \u2018iv\u2019 is maximum 1 year imprisonment or a fine or both.", " ", " What is an \u201cunwelcome and sexual overture\u201d?", " ", " What is unwelcome depends on the consent of the person who is being subjected to this \u2018overture\u2019. Something as simple as keeping one\u2019s hand on a woman\u2019s shoulder can be an unwelcome and sexual overture. However, there is nothing draconian about this. It is best to expressly ascertain and respect the personal physical boundaries set by every person.", " ", " Let us now take a step backwards in the chronological scheme of the Indian Penal Code and discuss Section 354 (as opposed to 354A) which talks about assault or criminal use of force coupled with \u201coutraging the modesty of a woman\u201d (punishment minimum 1 year, maximum 5 years imprisonment+ mandatory fine). What constitutes the \u201coutraging of modesty\u201d and how is it different from, for instance, \u201cphysical contact and advances involving explicit overtures\u201d? The act of assaulting and disrobing a woman used to be covered under Section 354, but it is now a separate crime under 354B after amendments in 2013.", " ", " Is the act of groping covered under Sections 354 or 354A?", " ", " In theory, the answer is that if there\u2019s an \u201cassault\u201d, it will fall under the former, if not, it falls under the latter. The purpose of this discussion regarding the difference between the two provisions is not to confound you with complicated legalese, but to mildly digress and point out that because several provisions appear to overlap and cover the same crime, corrupt cops often try to dupe a victim and draft the FIR in a manner that it results in registration of offences that attract lesser punishment.", " ", " The first thing that you must do while filing a complaint is to ensure that the incident is recorded in as much detail as possible. Insist on recording the incident in words that best describe the matter according to you and don\u2019t get persuaded by cops who insist on telling you what words/sentences to use. Pertinent to point out here that even if cops do have their way and record a distorted version of what happened, this can be challenged before the court.", " ", " Under Section 354B, the intentional act of assault/use of criminal force+disrobing a woman or the \u2018abetment\u2019 (enabling) of this act by someone else can lead to imprisonment of minimum 3 years and maximum 7 years, and a mandatory fine.", " ", " Another addition to the Indian Penal Code via the 2013 amendment is the offence of voyeurism. Watching, recording (photographs/video) a woman engaged in a \u2018private act\u2019 or the dissemination of such image/video(s) is punishable by imprisonment for minimum 1 year and maximum 3 years plus a mandatory fine when the offence is committed for the first time, and for a minimum 3 years and maximum 7 years for every subsequent offence. The phrase \u2018private act\u2019 includes acts where the \u201cvictim\u2019s genitals, posterior or breasts are exposed or covered only in underwear; the victim is using a lavatory; or the victim is doing a sexual act that is not of a kind ordinarily done in public\u201d.", " ", " Needless to add that as far as the mere act of recording is concerned, this offence gets invoked only if such recording is done without the consent of the victim and while the victim is engaged in such act in a private place where the victim has the reasonable expectation of privacy. For example, the mere act of \u2018recording\u2019 a person stripping and running on the streets is not an offence. If the victim has consented to the recording but not to the dissemination, this offence will get triggered.", " ", " Getting back to the issue of stalking. It is now a criminal offence, defined as the act of following a woman and contacting her, or attempting to, to initiate a personal interaction despite a clear expression of disinterest by the woman. In case there is any ambiguity over this, a woman saying \u201cno\u201d once is sufficiently \u201cexpressing disinterest\u201d. Stalking is punishable with maximum imprisonment of 3 years at the first commission of the offence and maximum 5 years at every subsequent commission.", " ", " A most welcome step has been the expansion of the definition of rape to include:", " ", " i) The act of inserting the penis not only in the vagina but also in the mouth, and/or urethra of a woman.", " ", " ii) Inserting any other part of the body into the anus, urethra or vagina of a woman.", " ", " iii) Applying the mouth to the vagina, urethra or the anus of a woman.", " ", " iv) Manipulating a woman\u2019s body in a manner to cause penetration in the anus, urethra or the vagina of the woman.", " ", " v) Compelling the woman to do any of the above acts with any other person.", " ", " The said acts are a crime only if they are done against the will or the consent of the woman. \u201cAgainst the will\u201d and \u201cwithout her consent\u201d are phrases used in the provision criminalising rape and the difference between the two is that the latter refers to situations where either consent is obtained by coercion or deceit. It is critical to note here that the absence of resistance by itself does not constitute consent. Without reproducing the letter of the law, I think it suffices to say that unless the woman", " expresses a firm and clear yes, please believe that consent is absent.", " ", " Shifting focus to the procedural aspects, it is critical to know that the registration of an FIR cannot be denied on grounds of \u2018territorial jurisdiction\u2019 \u2014 an excuse cops often use. They say they are helpless as the crime did not occur in their area. The truth is they are duty bound to register a case and if territorial jurisdiction is lacking, they register what is called a \u2018Zero-FIR\u2019, which is subsequently transferred to the relevant police station.", " ", " If the information about any of the aforementioned crimes (and many others such as throwing of acid) is given to the cops, their refusal to file an FIR can in fact land them in prison for a minimum period of 6 months and a maximum period of 2 years besides the payment of a mandatory fine. I often tell people that the moment cops refuse to register an FIR in any of the aforementioned cases, the first thing one should do is dial 100 and report that the police thana in question is refusing to lodge a case. You can also report the non-filing of the FIR to senior officers or to the nearest magistrate. If the victim is herself reporting the crime, the FIR must be mandatorily recorded by a woman police officer. If the victim is temporarily or permanently mentally or physically disabled, then the FIR must be recorded at the residence of the person who wants to report the offence or at a place convenient to the person. Moreover, this needs to be done in the presence of a special educator or an interpreter as the case maybe. In such cases, the process of recording the FIR must be video-graphed.", " ", " It is important to remember that the FIR need not necessarily be filed by the victim and can be filed by a bystander or any person requested to do so by the victim. The police have no business questioning the authority of the person filing the FIR. The officer writing the FIR is duty bound to read the FIR back to the complainant who must make sure that he/she has noted everything correctly. If not, then corrections must be made. Finally, the complainant is entitled to a free copy of the FIR.", " ", " The government of the day needs to do a lot more to make sure that more people are made aware about the provisions of such laws, failing which most of them will remain a dead letter."], "title": "In the line of FIR", "auth_datetime": ["Bangalore Mirror Bureau ", "|", " Updated: Jan 10, 2017, 04:00 IST"] }, { "url": "https://bangaloremirror.indiatimes.com/bangalore/crime/bangalore/crime/man-in-saudi-jail-for-carrying-epilepsy-meds/articleshow/56208607.cms", "content": [" \n", "\n", " \n", " \n", " \n", "\n", " \n", " \n", " A 35-year old man from ", ", Mangaluru has been languishing in a jail in ", " for over two months after he was detained at ", " airport for carrying a six-month stash of his epilepsy medicines without a doctor\u2019s prescription.\n", " \n", " His family, who came to know about his arrest about a week after he left, have been running pillar to post trying to get him out of prison. Police can exert tremendous power over female sex workers through the use of physical violence, harassment, unlawful arrests, forced detainment and forced or free sex, particularly in countries where sex work is criminalised. Effective HIV prevention programmes for female sex workers must address violence that is commonly experienced in their work environment,\u201d said the research team.", " ", " ", " Experts said that findings from epidemiological mapping estimate that approximately 1,30,000 female sex workers live and work in Karnataka. Although HIV prevalence among Karnataka\u2019s general population is low, at 0.5 per cent, female sex workers are disproportionately burdened by the HIV epidemic, with an estimated overall prevalence of 5.1 per cent in 2014, said officials involved with the programme.", " ", " ", " ", " ", " ", " ", " In Karnataka, the University of Manitoba and the Karnataka Health Promotion Trust (KHPT) were lead implementing partners for Avahan \u2013 the India AIDS Initiative of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. A series of district-level, integrated behavioural and biological assessment surveys were conducted among female sex workers in four districts of Karnataka: Bengaluru, Belagavi, Bellary and Shimoga. \u201cThis was done to examine trends in arrests over time, as well as associations between sex workers\u2019 characteristics and arrests, highlighting the need to focus on FSWs, who are disproportionately vulnerable to police arrest,\u201d said the authors.", " ", " ", " Structural interventions with police involved advocacy work with senior police officials, sensitisation workshops, and integration of HIV and human rights topics in pre-service curricula. \u201cDuring the workshops, officers were guided through the interpretation of existing laws that were being used to persecute female sex workers, educated about fundamental human rights and consequences of violating those rights, with specific reference to local sex work communities. BONDS AND PROMISES THAT DEFY ECONOMIC PRINCIPLES Experts say, any bonds that assure big growth can always be a trap and should be looked at critically. Growth rate \u2013 returns on investments made \u2013 will be astronomical and unrealistic, they add. \u201cSuch companies assure 25 to 35 percent growth on the investment, which is an outright lie. In India, the growth or insurance yield is around 6 percent and around 7 percent with taxes. Anything beyond that needs to be evaluated with a miscroscopic eye. Abroad, it is even less than that, may be around 2-3 per cent. If one does get promises of returns between 20-30 percent, consider it dubious ab initio. Such assurances are given by a set up of 8-10 people who claim to have taken a franchise of all insurance companies and offer to sell insurance policies of all kinds. People fall prey as such consultancies are in most cases not approved either by the company or run illegally without IRDA\u2019s approval.
